Writeups / Embedded & hardware security

Embedded & hardware security

Fault Injection and Side-Channel Studies

Planned experiments with voltage and clock glitching and power side-channel analysis, extending the existing RISC-V research with further investigation of physical attacks.

To be continued…

Planned scope

This planned series covers voltage and clock fault injection and DPA/CPA analysis using ChipWhisperer. The existing RISC-V baseline is documented separately; new experiments and hardware countermeasure comparisons remain planned.

Draft outline

This is a structured draft. Each section will be completed with measured results, commands, and evidence as the work is carried out.

Platform and controls

  • Reuse the PicoRV32/CW305 reference and matched controls.
  • Declare keys, budgets, and acceptance criteria before acquisition.
  • Record build and dataset identities.

Voltage and clock glitching

  • Sweep glitch width and offset within safe limits.
  • Record reset, lockup, and fault behavior.
  • Distinguish faults from invalid captures.

DPA and CPA extensions

  • Extend the first-round CPA baseline to further rounds and models.
  • Compare raw, aligned, and preprocessed analysis.
  • Report ranks, recovery effort, and success fractions.

Hardware countermeasures

  • Evaluate hiding, masking, shuffling, and scheduler candidates.
  • Use matched controls for every changed core or instruction path.
  • Record area, timing, power, and execution cost.

Evidence and limitations

  • Keep negative and inconclusive results.
  • State the tested budget for every non-recovery claim.
  • Link the experiment matrix and candidate study.
